memos.headline: S06 Stands Out as the Only Name Trading Above Its 200-Day Mean; S02 in Freefall
memos.body: I see a broad market bounce this week—most names up 5-10%—but the intermediate trend remains firmly down for the majority of the universe, with 8 of 10 names still below their 200-day averages. S06 is the clear relative-strength leader: it is the only ticker trading above its 200-day mean (+4.5%), has the shallowest drawdown from highs (-13.0%), and shows essentially flat 12-week relative strength vs SPY. S04 is the next-best setup, having reclaimed its 50-day mean (+1.2%) with positive 4-week relative strength (+3.2%), though it remains 5.7% below the 200-day. S02 is a broken chart—RSI at 27.7, down 33% from highs, 23.6% below its 200-day, and still making new lows last week (-7.8%)—and I see no reason to step in front of that. S07 and S03 show severe 12-week relative weakness vs SPY (-13.6% and -11.8% respectively) and remain deeply below their 200-day means, making them avoid candidates despite this week's bounce.

views.note: Only name above its 200-day mean with shallowest drawdown (-13%) and neutral 12w relative strength; would exit on a close below 230 (~200-day area).
Reclaimed 50-day mean with +3.2% 4w relative strength vs SPY; needs to clear ~415 (200-day zone) to gain conviction, would cut below 375.
RSI 27.7, down 33% from highs, -16.7% vs 50d mean, -15.9% 4w relative strength—textbook broken trend with no sign of stabilization.
Down 22.1% over 12w and 26w, 14.5% below 200-day, and -6.8% 4w relative strength vs SPY; bounce looks like a dead-cat rally unless 325 is reclaimed.
Worst 12w relative strength in the universe at -11.8% vs SPY despite a strong +9.5% weekly bounce; still 5.1% below 200-day and 21.9% off highs.
Flat 12w return and +8.4% 12w relative strength vs SPY suggest defensive character, but -5.0% 4w relative strength and middling RSI 50.5 offer no edge either way.
Close to 50-day mean (-1.4%) with decent 4w relative strength (+2.7%), but 21.5% drawdown and -8.6% 12w relative strength keep me on the sideline; would get interested above 170.
Strong +9.4% weekly bounce but still 11.6% below 200-day and 25.7% off highs with 7.36% ATR—too volatile and too far from trend to have conviction.

memos.headline: S10's 56% Net Margin and 78% Revenue Growth Stand Out; S02 and S09 Show Earnings-Power Weakness
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10, which posted $22.09B net income on $39.33B revenue (56.2% net margin) with YoY revenue growth of 77.9% and net income growth of 79.8%, all on just $8.46B of total debt—an exceptionally clean balance sheet. S05 also impresses with 27.5% net margins, 11.8% revenue growth, 28.3% net income growth, and only $14.79B in debt against $96.47B in revenue. On the other end, S02 delivered just 5.5% net margins on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B in debt and anemic 1.6% net income growth—I see no margin expansion catalyst here. S09 is similarly unattractive: revenue declined 1.1% YoY, net income slipped 0.3%, and the 9.1% margin on $83.43B revenue leaves little cushion if top-line pressure continues. I would revisit S02 and S09 only if operating margins inflect upward for two consecutive quarters.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, 78% revenue growth, minimal leverage ($8.46B debt) — the strongest earnings-power profile in the universe.
27.5% net margin with 28.3% NI growth and low debt-to-revenue ratio make this a high-quality compounder.
34.6% net margin and 12.3% revenue growth on $69.63B revenue; $44.97B debt is manageable given cash generation.
32.7% margin and 50.5% NI growth are strong, but $401.42B total debt demands careful monitoring of leverage ratios.
88.3% NI growth is impressive but off a low 10.7% margin base; sustainability of margin expansion is the key variable.
29.2% margin is solid but revenue grew only 4% YoY and $94.80B debt is elevated; need to see top-line reaccelerate.
19.1% margin is decent but revenue declined 2.1% YoY and NI was flat; would turn constructive on a return to growth.
Revenue fell 5.0% YoY to $16.21B with $31.74B debt nearly 2x revenue—leverage is uncomfortable on a shrinking top line.
Revenue -1.1%, NI -0.3%, 9.1% margin on $83.43B revenue with $36.76B debt—no earnings-power expansion visible.
5.5% net margin and only 1.6% NI growth on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B debt signals thin, fragile earnings power.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Growth Signals — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Staples Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, yet the 100bp of cuts over the past year and a steepening 10y-2y spread (+79bp YoY to +0.55pp) signal the market is pricing further easing ahead. CPI is running at 2.4% YoY — benign enough to keep the door open for cuts, but not low enough to force the Fed's hand imminently. The unemployment rate at 4.2% has drifted up 30bp over the past year, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than recession. The 10y yield falling 41bp YoY to 4.29% is a tailwind for duration-sensitive equities and a headwind for banks' net interest margins as the curve steepens from a low base. A surprise CPI print above 3% or a payrolls collapse below 100k would change my regime call from 'pause-trending-toward-easing' to something more extreme.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and a Fed leaning toward eventual easing.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment drifts higher and the slowdown regime favors low-beta sectors.
Banks face mixed signals: curve steepening helps NIM but slowing growth and potential further rate cuts compress front-end yields.
Cyclicals are vulnerable to the mild slowdown signaled by rising unemployment and a Fed still on hold rather than stimulating.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; moderate CPI and a slowing economy suggest range-bound demand conditions.
Rate-sensitive sectors like real estate or utilities benefit as the 10y yield drops 34bp over three months.

memos.headline: S02 Sentiment Collapse Dominates; S06 and S05 Show Positive Tone Inflection Post-Earnings
memos.body: I am reading the event-driven sentiment signals across the universe as of April 25. The standout negative is S02, which printed a -22.4% price reaction on its April 17 earnings 8-K — a sentiment shock of that magnitude typically takes weeks to digest and suggests further negative narrative overhang. S01 also disappointed with a -3.7% move on its Q3 FY25 earnings release on April 24, signaling a tone shift lower that may not yet be fully priced given the recency. On the positive side, S06 posted a +4.0% reaction to its April 11 earnings and followed up with additional 8-K filings through April 22, suggesting sustained constructive narrative flow. S05 saw a modest +1.7% lift on its April 24 earnings 8-K, a mildly positive tone turn that I view as incremental rather than decisive. I have lower conviction on names like S07, S09, and S10 where filings are largely procedural (director changes, Reg FD) with no observable price catalysts.

views.note: A -22.4% earnings-day collapse signals deeply negative sentiment that is unlikely to reverse quickly.
Positive +4.0% earnings reaction and continued 8-K activity through April 22 suggest constructive narrative momentum.
Modest +1.7% post-earnings lift on April 24 is a mild positive tone turn but not yet a strong signal.
Fresh -3.7% earnings reaction on April 24 indicates a negative tone shift that likely has not been fully absorbed.
Two director-change 8-Ks in April are procedural with no observable sentiment catalyst.
Early-April filings are routine (director change, Reg FD) with no price reaction data to gauge tone.
Sparse filing activity and no earnings event leave sentiment direction unclear.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surge and Falling Oil Signal Structural Geopolitical Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I see a macro backdrop dominated by geopolitical and policy risk: the economic policy uncertainty index sits at 419.9, up 122% over three months, while VIX has spiked 78% over the same window to 26.47—both consistent with an escalating tariff/sanctions regime rather than a one-quarter blip. High-yield OAS widening of +113 bp over three months to 3.73% tells me credit markets are pricing durable stress, not just sentiment noise. WTI crude at $63.55, down 15% in three months, suggests demand destruction fears outweigh any supply-side geopolitical premium, which is unusual and points to trade-war drag on global growth. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy cross-border supply-chain exposure (S06, S10) face structural headwinds, while domestically oriented or energy-cost-sensitive names (S05, S01) may benefit from lower input costs, though the uncertainty premium keeps me cautious everywhere. A reversal in tariff policy or a credible US-China de-escalation framework would change my view materially.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in two weeks during peak policy uncertainty suggest the company is actively managing geopolitical exposure; elevated HY OAS and VIX argue for caution on globally exposed names.
Mid-April 8-K during a period of 122% 3m rise in policy uncertainty raises concern about export-control or supply-chain disruption risk.
Frequent 8-K disclosures suggest active corporate communication; falling WTI could ease input costs, but the extreme uncertainty environment caps upside conviction.
Two Reg FD filings in April hint at proactive investor engagement; lower oil prices are a tailwind, but VIX at 26.5 and wide HY spreads keep me from going long.
Early-April 8-K filings preceded the worst of the uncertainty spike; without clarity on the company's tariff/sanctions exposure I stay neutral.
Single Reg FD filing on April 10 offers limited signal; the broader macro stress environment warrants caution but no directional call.

plan.summary: Elevated policy uncertainty (EPU +122%, VIX 26.5, HY OAS widening) and most names still below 200-day averages argue for a cautious, high-cash posture. We concentrate in the few names where multiple analysts agree on quality and relative strength—S04, S06, S05—and take a smaller position in S10 on exceptional fundamentals despite technical and geopolitical headwinds.

plans.rationale: Three-way agreement: Technical (reclaimed 50d, +3.2% 4w RS), Fundamentals (34.6% net margin, 12.3% rev growth), and Macro (defensive staples positioning in slowdown). Sizing near max given broad analyst alignment.
plans.changes_my_mind: Fails to hold above 375 (roughly 4.5% stop) or weekly close back below 50-day mean, signaling the bounce was a dead-cat rally.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst's top pick—only name above 200d mean with shallowest drawdown. Sentiment confirms positive earnings reaction (+4.0%). Sized down from seed because Geopolitics analyst flags cross-border risk and Fundamentals notes $401B debt load.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 230 (200-day area, ~5.5% stop) or a new tariff action specifically targeting financial services cross-border flows.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's second-highest conviction long (27.5% margin, 28.3% NI growth, low leverage). Sentiment mildly positive post-earnings (+1.7%). Technical is neutral but notes decent 4w RS (+2.7%). Geopolitics notes falling oil as input-cost tailwind. Sized moderately given technical ambiguity.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 152 (~6% stop) or next quarter's margins compress below 25%, invalidating the compounder thesis.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's highest-conviction name (56% net margin, 78% rev growth, minimal debt). Macro analyst sees rate-sensitive tailwind from falling 10y yields. However, Technical flags extreme volatility (7.4% ATR) and 11.6% below 200d, while Geopolitics warns of export-control risk. Sized small with wide stop to respect volatility.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 100 (~10% stop) or any new US export-control action targeting the semiconductor/AI supply chain.

orders.note: Strong 1w rally (+6.5%) into elevated vol; use shallow limit to avoid chasing. ATR ~4% of price, gap filter at 3%.
Up ~5% on the week with ATR ~4.3% of price; modest pullback limit to improve fill price in choppy tape.
Biggest 1w return (+7.1%) among the core trio; higher avg gap (~1.15%) warrants slightly deeper limit offset and gap guard.
Strongest 1w move (+9.4%), highest avg gap (~2%), and geopolitical headwinds noted in plan. Deeper limit and wider gap filter to manage execution risk on a smaller position.

execution.notes: All four names rallied sharply last week into a still-elevated VIX/EPU environment. Limit orders give us a chance to enter on intraday pullbacks rather than chasing momentum. Gap filters protect against opening spikes that would erode edge. If limits don't fill early in the week, reassess mid-week.
